PROACTIVE STREAMING VIDEO UNDERSTANDING

SVUBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Proactive Streaming Video Understanding

TL;DR

Understand events as they unfold, respond at the right time, and recover relevant history. SVUBench evaluates these capabilities with ten proactive tasks, Basic and Trajectory modes, and the Proactive Response Score.

THE BENCHMARK

Abstract

Proactive streaming video understanding requires models to interpret unfolding events, respond timely, and retrieve relevant historical evidence. To systematically evaluate these capabilities, we introduce SVUBench, a comprehensive proactive streaming video benchmark comprising 12,131 questions and 62,881 answer points across ten proactive tasks spanning Perception, Understanding, and Reasoning. Constructed through model-assisted annotation and human verification, SVUBench introduces two complementary interaction modes. Basic evaluates sustained proactive responses from video onset, while Trajectory requires historical recovery and continuous response updates following task activation during streaming. A Duration-Scaled Challenge further evaluates these capabilities across four video duration tiers. We develop the Proactive Response Score (PRS) with task-adaptive answer windows to jointly assess answer correctness, response timeliness, historical consistency, and content quality. Extensive experiments and analysis reveal the strengths and limitations of existing models, highlighting directions for advancing proactive streaming video understanding.

PERCEPTION · UNDERSTANDING · REASONING

Ten tasks. A continuously unfolding world.

From recognizing visual attributes to integrating long histories and anticipating what happens next.

DUAL INTERACTION MODES

Monitor continuously. Retrieve and update.

Basic

Sustained proactive responses

The task is activated at video onset and remains active throughout the stream. Models provide the Current Answer when sufficient evidence becomes available, then update their responses as new events emerge.

Task at onsetCurrent AnswerUpdated Answer
Trajectory

Historical recovery and continuous updates

The task is introduced midway through the video. The first valid response includes the Current Answer + Historical Trace; later responses include the Current Answer + Last Evidence.

OUR SCORING METHOD

Proactive Response Score

Answer correctness, response timeliness, historical consistency, and content quality in one evaluation framework.

Task-adaptive temporal scoring

Each target event \(i\) has a valid response window \(W_i\), with start \(a_i\) and deadline \(b_i\). Earlier responses within the window receive higher temporal scores.

\[T_i(t)=\begin{cases}10^{-(t-a_i)/\tau_i},&t\in W_i,\\0,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\qquad \tau_i=\min\{\max(\ell_i,\Delta),\,b_i-a_i\}.\]

Here, \(\ell_i\) is the local event duration and \(\Delta\) is the video sampling interval. Response time is determined by the last observed frame when generation begins. The first available response slot within each valid window receives no temporal penalty.

Answer windows by task

Let \([s_i,e_i]\) be the evidence interval, \(T\) the clip end, and \(n_i=\min(s_{i+1},T)\), with \(n_i=T\) for the last event. Future Prediction additionally uses a cue interval \([c_i^s,c_i^e]\).

TasksValid response window
Attribute Perception, Action Perception, Spatial Relation Perception, State Transition Recognition, Pattern Recognition\([s_i,\min(e_i,n_i))\)
Event Counting\([e_i,n_i]\)
Spatiotemporal Reasoning, Causal Reasoning\([e_i,n_i)\)
Future Prediction\([c_i^s,\min(c_i^e,s_i,T))\)

Windows ending at \(T\) include this endpoint; Future Prediction always excludes target onset \(s_i\). A window with no response opportunity may extend to the next available online opportunity within its hard boundaries. Overlapping windows assign a response to the event with the latest window onset, with ties resolved by event order.

From response quality to event utility

For the \(m_i\) responses within \(W_i\), let \(d_{ij}=T_i(t_{ij})\) and \(d_{i,m_i+1}=0\). The event utility and normalized run score are

\[U_i=\sum_{j=1}^{m_i}Q_{ij}(d_{ij}-d_{i,j+1}),\qquad S_{\mathrm{run}}=100\cdot\frac{2\sum_{i=1}^{N}U_i}{N+M}.\]

\(N\) is the number of reference events and \(M\) is the number of submitted responses. All submitted responses, including incorrect, repeated, and out-of-window outputs, contribute to \(M\).

Basic response quality

\[Q_{ij}^{\mathrm{Basic}}=C_{ij},\quad C_{ij}\in\{0,1\}.\]

Response quality is the correctness of the current answer.

Trajectory response quality

\[H_{ij}=\frac{2Z_{ij}}{K_{ij}+P_{ij}},\quad Q_{ij}^{\mathrm{Traj}}=C_{ij}\frac{1+H_{ij}}{2}.\]

\(K_{ij}\) and \(P_{ij}\) count reference and predicted historical events. Order-preserving, one-to-one matching maximizes total credit \(Z_{ij}\). A semantic match receives 1 if its timestamp falls within the reference evidence window, and 0.5 otherwise. Set \(H_{ij}=1\) when \(K_{ij}+P_{ij}=0\).

PROACTIVE SUMMARIZATION

Local detail. Cumulative memory. Global synthesis.

A fixed judging prompt assigns semantic quality scores in {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1}.

Current Caption and Final Summary

Each output is assigned to at most one annotated segment by its timestamp. The first available response opportunity after a segment ends preferentially matches that segment. Each segment uses its last complete caption in the corresponding segment window. The Final Summary is evaluated separately against the global video reference.

\[S_{\mathrm{cap}}^{\mathrm{Basic}}=100\cdot\frac{2\sum_{i=1}^{n}Q_i^{\mathrm{last}}}{n+M_{\mathrm{cap}}},\qquad S_F^{\mathrm{Basic}}=100\cdot Q_F,\qquad S_{\mathrm{CS}}^{\mathrm{Basic}}=\frac{S_{\mathrm{cap}}^{\mathrm{Basic}}+S_F^{\mathrm{Basic}}}{2}.\]

Cumulative Caption in Trajectory

The first valid response after activation jointly provides a Current Caption and a Cumulative Caption covering the clip start through the current segment. Later responses provide segment captions, followed by a Final Summary at video completion. Let \(Q_A^{\mathrm{last}}\) be cumulative quality in the last complete submission within the first response window, and \(M_A\) its number of submissions.

\[S_A=100\cdot\frac{2Q_A^{\mathrm{last}}}{1+M_A},\qquad S_{\mathrm{CS}}^{\mathrm{Traj}}=\frac{2S_A+S_{\mathrm{cap}}^{\mathrm{Traj}}+S_F^{\mathrm{Traj}}}{4}.\]

\(S_{\mathrm{cap}}^{\mathrm{Traj}}\) evaluates current captions from the first valid segment onward. \(S_F^{\mathrm{Traj}}\) evaluates the final summary of the entire clip, including observations before activation.

DATASET CONSTRUCTION

Model-assisted annotation, human verification.

Candidate video curation, temporal sample reconstruction, and quality control yield 3,398 verified samples from 2,775 videos.
